# Overview

This document provides function-by-function documentation for the `chFnirs` package. The package provides helper functions for second-level (group-level) analysis of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data: unified wrappers for area-wise linear and mixed-model omnibus tests, `emmeans`-based activation tests and post-hoc contrasts, slope-based continuous-moderator analyses, Benjamini--Hochberg FDR correction, and p-value / effect-size / beta heatmap generation.

All analysis functions are designed to operate on long-format tables of per-subject, per-channel (or per-region) response estimates produced by any fNIRS first-level pipeline.

## Function hierarchy

The package contains 26 exported functions (plus 1 internal helper) organized into five layers:

| Layer | Functions | Role |
|-------|----------|------|
| **Omnibus testing** | `run_omnibus_by_area`, `run_omnibus_by_area_bh` | Area-wise Type III ANOVA with optional robust covariance and BH correction |
| **Activation & slopes** | `run_activation_tests`, `run_slopes_vs_zero` | Ungated marginal-mean and slope-vs-zero tests |
| **Gated post-hocs** | `run_gated_posthoc`, `run_gated_slopes` | Pairwise contrasts gated on omnibus significance |
| **Visualization** | `createHeatMapsFromLmerAreaAnalysis`, `CreateSigBetaTable`, `create_pvalue_heatmap`, `create_posthoc_heatmap`, `create_omnibus_heatmap`, `create_forced_color_heatmap`, `create_effect_size_heatmap`, `create_heatmap_legend`, `plot_simple_slopes`, `plot_slope_lines` | Heatmaps, standalone legends, and slope plots |
| **Utilities** | `getBHvalues`, `getQvalues`, `compute_cohens_d`, `compute_partial_eta_sq`, `has_tested_results`, `standardize_emmeans_columns`, `write_results_by_type`, `sort_rois_anatomically`, `sort_fnirs_channels_by_name`, `heatmap_height`, `shorten_string`, `run_lmer_analysis_by_area` (deprecated) | Effect sizes, p-value adjustment, column renaming, I/O, sorting, sizing |
| **Internal** | `iterate_by_area` | Shared iteration engine for the area-wise analysis functions |

## Output column schema

All area-wise analysis functions produce output in a unified snake\_case schema:

**Identifier columns (all functions):** `type`, `area`.

**Omnibus:** `effect`, `statistic`, `statistic_type` (`"F"`), `df_num`, `df_den`, `p_value`, `partial_eta_sq`, and (after BH) `p_bh`.

**Activation / slopes-vs-zero:** `predictor`, `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `statistic`, `statistic_type` (`"t"` or `"z"`), `p_value`, `cohens_d`.

**Gated post-hocs:** `contrast`, `predictor`, `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `statistic`, `statistic_type` (`"t"`), `p_bon`, `cohens_d`.

**Gated slopes additionally:** `omnibus_effect`, `posthoc_type`.

## Common arguments

Several arguments are shared across the area-wise analysis functions:

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `data` | data.frame | Long-format data with one row per subject x type x area x condition. |
| `formula` | formula or string | Model formula. Formula objects preferred; character strings silently coerced. |
| `area_col` | string | Column naming the brain area (e.g., `"ROI"`, `"Channel"`). |
| `type_col` | string | Column naming the measurement type (chromophore). Default: `"type"`. |
| `model` | string | Required, no default. `"lmer"` for linear mixed models, `"lm"` for ordinary linear models. |
| `vcov` | string or NULL | Covariance estimator. NULL resolves to `"classical"` for lmer, `"HC3"` for lm. Options: `"classical"`, `"HC0"`--`"HC5"`. HC with lmer raises an error. |
| `min_rows` | integer | Minimum cell size; smaller cells are silently skipped. Default: 5. |

\newpage

# Omnibus testing

## `run_omnibus_by_area`

Fits a linear or linear mixed model to every unique combination of measurement type and area, runs a Type III ANOVA on each fit, and returns a long-format table with one row per effect x type x area combination.

### Usage

```{r}
run_omnibus_by_area(
  data,
  formula,
  area_col,
  type_col = "type",
  model,
  vcov = NULL,
  min_rows = 5,
  effect_size = TRUE
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `data` | data.frame | | Long-format data. |
| `formula` | formula/string | | Model formula. |
| `area_col` | string | | Area column name. |
| `type_col` | string | `"type"` | Measurement-type column. |
| `model` | string | *required* | `"lmer"` or `"lm"`. |
| `vcov` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Covariance estimator. NULL resolves to `"classical"` (lmer) or `"HC3"` (lm). |
| `min_rows` | integer | `5` | Minimum observations per cell. |
| `effect_size` | logical | `TRUE` | Always includes `partial_eta_sq` column; `NA_real_` for lmer. |

### Return value

Data frame with columns: `type`, `area`, `effect`, `statistic`, `statistic_type` (`"F"`), `df_num`, `df_den`, `p_value`, `partial_eta_sq`. Returns `NULL` if no cell produced output.

### Details

**On the choice of HC estimator.** HC0--HC5 are heteroscedasticity-consistent (sandwich) covariance estimators. HC3 divides each squared residual by $(1 - h_{ii})^2$ and is approximately a jackknife estimator. Long and Ervin (2000) showed HC3 has the best small-sample properties among HC0--HC3, which is why it is the resolved default when `model = "lm"`.

**Why HC estimators do not apply to lmer models.** HC estimators are defined against the OLS hat matrix and residual structure. Linear mixed models do not have a hat matrix in the same sense. Passing any HC value with `model = "lmer"` raises an explicit error directing the user to either set `vcov = "classical"` or switch to `model = "lm"`.

### Example

```{r}
df.omnibus <- run_omnibus_by_area(
  data     = df.all,
  formula  = estimate ~ Group * cond + (1 | ID),
  area_col = "ROI",
  model    = "lmer"
)
```

\newpage

## `run_omnibus_by_area_bh`

Convenience wrapper that chains `run_omnibus_by_area()` with `getBHvalues()` so that the common "fit omnibus, then BH-correct" sequence is a single call. The result is identical to calling the two functions in sequence.

### Usage

```{r}
run_omnibus_by_area_bh(
  data,
  formula,
  area_col,
  type_col       = "type",
  model,
  vcov           = NULL,
  min_rows       = 5,
  effect_size    = TRUE,
  bh_group_col   = c("type", "effect"),
  bh_p_val_col   = "p_value"
)
```

### Arguments

All arguments from `run_omnibus_by_area`, plus:

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `bh_group_col` | character vector | `c("type", "effect")` | Column(s) defining independent BH correction families. |
| `bh_p_val_col` | string | `"p_value"` | Raw p-value column to correct. |

### Return value

The omnibus table with an added `p_bh` column. Returns `NULL` if the underlying omnibus call produced no output.

### Example

```{r}
# Two-line "omnibus + BH + gated post-hoc" pattern:
df.omnibus <- run_omnibus_by_area_bh(
  data     = df.all,
  formula  = estimate ~ Group * cond + (1 | ID),
  area_col = "ROI",
  model    = "lmer"
)
df.ph.group <- run_gated_posthoc(
  omnibus_df      = df.omnibus,
  effect_name     = "Group",
  data            = df.all,
  formula         = estimate ~ Group * cond + (1 | ID),
  area_col        = "ROI",
  contrast_factor = "Group",
  model           = "lmer"
)
```

\newpage

# Activation and slope tests

## `run_activation_tests`

For each type x area cell, fits the model and computes marginal means at each level of `by_factor` via `emmeans::emmeans()`, then tests each marginal mean against zero. The "activation from baseline" test for categorical designs.

### Usage

```{r}
run_activation_tests(
  data,
  formula,
  area_col,
  by_factor,
  type_col  = "type",
  model,
  vcov      = NULL,
  min_rows  = 5,
  cohens_d  = TRUE
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `by_factor` | string | | Factor whose marginal means are tested (e.g., `"Group"`, `"cond"`). |
| `cohens_d` | logical | `TRUE` | Always includes a `cohens_d` column via `compute_cohens_d()`. |

All other arguments are the common set described in Section 1.3.

### Return value

Data frame with columns: `type`, `area`, `predictor`, `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `statistic`, `statistic_type` (`"t"` or `"z"`), `p_value`, `cohens_d`. Returns `NULL` if no cell produced output.

### Example

```{r}
df.activ <- run_activation_tests(
  data      = df.all,
  formula   = estimate ~ Group * cond + (1 | ID),
  area_col  = "ROI",
  by_factor = "Group",
  model     = "lmer"
)
```

\newpage

## `run_slopes_vs_zero`

For each type x area cell, fits the model and uses `emmeans::emtrends()` to compute the slope of a continuous moderator (`trend_var`), then tests each slope against zero. The continuous-moderator analog of `run_activation_tests()`.

### Usage

```{r}
run_slopes_vs_zero(
  data,
  formula,
  area_col,
  trend_var,
  by_factor = NULL,
  type_col  = "type",
  model,
  vcov      = NULL,
  min_rows  = 5,
  cohens_d  = TRUE
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `trend_var` | string | | Continuous moderator whose slope is tested (e.g., `"cortisol"`). Must appear in `formula`. |
| `by_factor` | string/NULL | `NULL` | If NULL, tests a single overall slope per cell. If a factor name, tests a slope within each level. |

### Return value

Data frame with columns: `type`, `area`, `predictor`, `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `statistic`, `statistic_type` (`"t"`), `p_value`, `cohens_d`. The `predictor` column is labeled `"<trend_var>_Slope"` (overall) or `"<level>_<trend_var>_Slope"` (within `by_factor`).

### Example

```{r}
df.slopes <- run_slopes_vs_zero(
  data      = df.all,
  formula   = estimate ~ Group * cond * cortisol + (1 | ID),
  area_col  = "ROI",
  trend_var = "cortisol",
  by_factor = "Group",
  model     = "lmer"
)
```

\newpage

# Gated post-hoc contrasts

## `run_gated_posthoc`

For each type x area cell, checks whether a named omnibus effect passed the significance gate, and if so, runs pairwise Bonferroni-adjusted contrasts via `emmeans::contrast()`. Non-significant cells optionally receive NA-filled placeholder rows for grey heatmap tiles.

### Usage

```{r}
run_gated_posthoc(
  omnibus_df,
  effect_name,
  data,
  formula,
  area_col,
  contrast_factor,
  by_var       = NULL,
  type_col     = "type",
  model,
  vcov         = NULL,
  p_col        = "p_bh",
  p_threshold  = 0.05,
  fill_empty   = TRUE,
  min_rows     = 5,
  cohens_d     = TRUE,
  adjust       = "bonferroni"
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `omnibus_df` | data.frame | | Output of `run_omnibus_by_area_bh()`. Must contain `p_col`. |
| `effect_name` | string | | Omnibus effect to gate on (e.g., `"Group"`, `"Group:cond"`). |
| `contrast_factor` | string | | Factor to contrast over (e.g., `"Group"`). |
| `by_var` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Nesting factor for conditional contrasts (e.g., `"cond"`). |
| `p_col` | string | `"p_bh"` | Column in `omnibus_df` to gate on. Errors if missing. |
| `p_threshold` | numeric | `0.05` | Gate threshold. |
| `fill_empty` | logical | `TRUE` | NA-fill non-significant cells for grey heatmap tiles. |
| `adjust` | string | `"bonferroni"` | Passed to `emmeans::contrast()`. Output column is always `p_bon`. |

### Return value

Data frame with columns: `type`, `area`, `contrast`, `predictor`, `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `statistic`, `statistic_type` (`"t"`), `p_bon`, `cohens_d`.

### Example

```{r}
df.posthoc <- run_gated_posthoc(
  omnibus_df      = df.omnibus,
  effect_name     = "Group:cond",
  data            = df.all,
  formula         = estimate ~ Group * cond + (1 | ID),
  area_col        = "ROI",
  contrast_factor = "Group",
  by_var          = "cond",
  model           = "lmer"
)
```

\newpage

## `run_gated_slopes`

For each type x area cell, checks gated significance of every omnibus effect involving a continuous moderator and, for those that pass, runs pairwise Bonferroni-adjusted slope comparisons via `emmeans::emtrends()` + `emmeans::contrast()`. Automatically decomposes interactions based on `categorical_factors`.

### Usage

```{r}
run_gated_slopes(
  omnibus_df,
  data,
  formula,
  area_col,
  trend_var,
  categorical_factors,
  effect_pattern = trend_var,
  type_col       = "type",
  model,
  vcov           = NULL,
  p_col          = "p_bh",
  p_threshold    = 0.05,
  fill_empty     = TRUE,
  min_rows       = 5,
  cohens_d       = TRUE,
  adjust         = "bonferroni",
  suffix         = "SlopeDiff"
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `trend_var` | string | | Continuous moderator whose slopes are compared. |
| `categorical_factors` | character vector | | Categorical factors in the design (e.g., `c("Group", "cond")`). Used to decompose interactions. |
| `effect_pattern` | string | `trend_var` | Regex for selecting slope-containing effects from `omnibus_df`. |
| `suffix` | string | `"SlopeDiff"` | Appended to predictor labels to distinguish slope from mean comparisons. |

### Return value

Data frame with columns: `type`, `area`, `omnibus_effect`, `posthoc_type`, `contrast`, `predictor`, `estimate`, `se`, `df`, `statistic`, `statistic_type` (`"t"`), `p_bon`, `cohens_d`.

### Decomposition rules

For each matching omnibus effect, the function inspects the effect name via `grepl()` against `categorical_factors`:

- **No categorical factors in effect** (e.g., just `trend_var`): single overall slope vs zero.
- **One categorical factor** (e.g., `Group:trend_var`): pairwise slope comparison across that factor.
- **Two categorical factors** (e.g., `Group:cond:trend_var`): decomposed into both conditional slicings (`~ Group | cond` and `~ cond | Group`), tagged with Title Case `posthoc_type` labels (e.g., `"GroupByCond"`, `"CondByGroup"`).

### Example

```{r}
# Filter omnibus to slope effects, then run gated slopes
df.omnibus.h <- df.omnibus.h.full[grepl(hVar, df.omnibus.h.full$effect), ]
df.h.posthoc <- run_gated_slopes(
  omnibus_df          = df.omnibus.h,
  data                = df.all,
  formula             = h_formula,
  area_col            = "ROI",
  trend_var           = hVar,
  categorical_factors = c("Group", "cond"),
  model               = "lmer"
)
```

\newpage

# Visualization

## `createHeatMapsFromLmerAreaAnalysis`

High-level wrapper that generates heatmaps and CSV files from model results. Dispatches to `CreateSigBetaTable` for reshaping and then to the appropriate heatmap function based on `heatmap_type`. Supports per-type subdirectory output and a caller-supplied x-axis ordering via `area_order` (see "Pluggable area sorters" below).

### Usage

```{r}
createHeatMapsFromLmerAreaAnalysis(
  results_df, area_col, group_col, sigValue_col,
  dv_col         = "Beta",
  area_order     = NULL,
  output_prefix  = NULL,
  output_dir     = ".",
  split_by_type  = TRUE,
  type_col       = "type",
  significance_threshold = 0.05,
  heatmap_type   = "posthoc",
  scale_type     = "log",
  log_power      = 0.2,
  asterisk_sz    = 10,
  fig_width      = 11,
  fig_height     = 8.5,
  show_legend    = TRUE,
  removeIntercept = TRUE
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `results_df` | data.frame | | Long-format model results. |
| `area_col` | string | | Area column name. |
| `group_col` | string/NULL | | Column to group by (e.g., `"type"`). |
| `sigValue_col` | string | | Corrected p-value column. |
| `dv_col` | string | `"Beta"` | Column whose sign gives effect direction. |
| `area_order` | char vec/NULL | `NULL` | Desired x-axis order. Precompute with `sort_rois_anatomically()` (ROIs) or `sort_fnirs_channels_by_name()` (channels). `NULL` = order of occurrence. |
| `output_prefix` | string | `NULL` | Base name for output files. |
| `output_dir` | string | `"."` | Parent output directory. |
| `split_by_type` | logical | `TRUE` | Write per-type subdirectories. |
| `heatmap_type` | string | `"posthoc"` | `"omnibus"`, `"posthoc"`, or `"activation"`. |
| `scale_type` | string | `"log"` | `"log"` or `"linear"`. |
| `log_power` | numeric | `0.2` | Controls log scale intensity. |
| `asterisk_sz` | numeric | `10` | Asterisk size in mm. |
| `fig_width` | numeric | `11` | Figure width in inches, forwarded to all primitive heatmap calls. |
| `fig_height` | numeric | `8.5` | Figure height in inches, forwarded to all primitive heatmap calls. |
| `show_legend` | logical | `TRUE` | Forward to all primitive heatmap calls. `FALSE` suppresses the legend on every sub-heatmap, for use with `create_heatmap_legend()` in publication panels. |
| `removeIntercept` | logical | `TRUE` | Drop intercept rows. |

### Return value

Nothing. Writes CSVs and PDFs under `output_dir`.

\newpage

## `CreateSigBetaTable`

Reshapes a long-format data frame of model results into a wide-format `predictor x area` table suitable for heatmap rendering. Supports three output modes: `"discrete"` (-1, 0, 1), `"continuous_signed"` (signed p-value), and `"continuous_unsigned"` (absolute p-value).

### Usage

```{r}
CreateSigBetaTable(
  df.data,
  areaColName     = "area",
  sigColName,
  dv_col          = "estimate",
  predColName     = NULL,
  group_col       = NULL,
  output_mode     = "discrete",
  sigThresh       = 0.05,
  removeIntercept = TRUE
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `df.data` | data.frame | | Long-format model results. |
| `areaColName` | string | `"area"` | Area column name. |
| `sigColName` | string | *required* | Significance column (e.g., `"p_bh"`, `"p_bon"`). |
| `dv_col` | string | `"estimate"` | Column whose sign gives effect direction. |
| `predColName` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Predictor column. Auto-detects `"predictor"` then `"Predictor"`. |
| `group_col` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Split column (e.g., `"type"`). |
| `output_mode` | string/logical | `"discrete"` | `"discrete"`, `"continuous_signed"`, or `"continuous_unsigned"`. |
| `sigThresh` | numeric | `0.05` | Threshold for discrete mode. |
| `removeIntercept` | logical | `TRUE` | Drop intercept rows. |

### Return value

Named list of wide data frames, one per level of `group_col` (or one named `"all_data"`).

\newpage

## `create_effect_size_heatmap`

Draws one heatmap of effect-size values (e.g., Cohen's d, partial eta-squared) per level of an optional grouping column. Uses a diverging blue--white--red palette when values include negatives (centered at zero), otherwise a sequential white--orange palette. Supports optional significance asterisks, numeric value labels, and a caller-supplied x-axis ordering via `area_order` (see "Pluggable area sorters" below).

### Usage

```{r}
create_effect_size_heatmap(
  results_df,
  area_col,
  es_col,
  p_col              = NULL,
  significance_threshold = 0.05,
  asterisk_size      = 6,
  show_values        = TRUE,
  area_order         = NULL,
  group_col          = NULL,
  title              = NULL,
  low_color          = "blue",
  mid_color          = "white",
  high_color         = "red",
  seq_low_color      = "white",
  seq_high_color     = "darkorange",
  neg_label_digits   = 2,
  pos_label_digits   = 3,
  save_dir           = ".",
  file_prefix        = "EffectSize",
  fig_width          = 11,
  fig_height         = 8.5,
  landscape          = FALSE,
  split_by_type      = TRUE,
  show_legend        = TRUE,
  value_limits       = NULL,
  legend_breaks      = NULL,
  pos_legend_title   = NULL,
  neg_legend_title   = NULL
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `results_df` | data.frame | | Long-format results with `predictor`, `area_col`, and `es_col`. |
| `area_col` | string | | Area column (x-axis). |
| `es_col` | string | | Effect-size column (e.g., `"cohens_d"`, `"partial_eta_sq"`). |
| `p_col` | string/NULL | `NULL` | P-value column for asterisks. NULL = no asterisks. |
| `significance_threshold` | numeric | `0.05` | P-value threshold for asterisks. |
| `asterisk_size` | numeric | `6` | Asterisk size in mm. |
| `show_values` | logical | `TRUE` | Print numeric effect sizes in cells. |
| `area_order` | char vec/NULL | `NULL` | Desired x-axis order. Precompute with `sort_rois_anatomically()` (ROIs) or `sort_fnirs_channels_by_name()` (channels). `NULL` = order of occurrence. |
| `group_col` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Split column (one heatmap per group). |
| `split_by_type` | logical | `TRUE` | Route per-group PDFs to subdirectories. |
| `show_legend` | logical | `TRUE` | If `FALSE`, suppress the fill-scale legend (for publication panels paired with `create_heatmap_legend()`). |
| `value_limits` | numeric/NULL | `NULL` | Colorbar domain. For Cohen's d-style diverging data, pass `c(-1, 1)` (or wider). For partial η², pass `c(0, 0.2)`. `NULL` = auto from data range. There is no universal default. |
| `legend_breaks` | numeric/NULL | `NULL` | Tick positions on the colorbar. Diverging palettes auto-route negative values to the negative bar. `NULL` = ggplot default. |
| `pos_legend_title` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Title for the positive colorbar (diverging) or sole colorbar (sequential). `NULL` = `es_col`. |
| `neg_legend_title` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Title for the negative colorbar (diverging only). `NULL` = `es_col`. |

### Diverging vs sequential

The function chooses palette automatically based on whether `es_col` contains negative values:

- **Diverging** (any negatives, e.g. Cohen's d): two split colorbars (`mid_color → high_color` for positive, `low_color → mid_color` for negative), joined with `ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()`. Mirrors the structure of `create_pvalue_heatmap` / `create_posthoc_heatmap`.
- **Sequential** (all non-negative, e.g. partial η²): single colorbar `seq_low_color → seq_high_color`.

### Label modes

The four cell-label modes are controlled by `show_values` and `p_col`:

| `show_values` | `p_col` | Result |
|:---:|:---:|:---|
| `TRUE` | `NULL` | Values only (default) |
| `TRUE` | non-NULL | Values with asterisks on significant cells |
| `FALSE` | non-NULL | Asterisks only |
| `FALSE` | `NULL` | No text |

### Example

```{r}
# Asterisks only, anatomically sorted ROIs
roi_order <- sort_rois_anatomically(unique(df.activation$area))

create_effect_size_heatmap(
  results_df  = df.activation,
  area_col    = "area",
  es_col      = "cohens_d",
  p_col       = "p_bh",
  show_values = FALSE,
  area_order  = roi_order,
  group_col   = "type",
  file_prefix = "Activation_byCond"
)
```

\newpage

## `create_pvalue_heatmap`

Generates a continuous heatmap for signed p-values (range -1 to 1) with split red/blue legends for positive and negative effects. Supports linear or log-style scaling and significance asterisks.

### Usage

```{r}
create_pvalue_heatmap(
  table_data,
  data_col_indices,
  descriptor_col_indices,
  scale_type             = "linear",
  log_power              = 0.2,
  legend_breaks          = c(-0.05, -0.01, -0.001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05),
  significance_threshold = 0.05,
  asterisk_size          = 6,
  pos_legend_title       = "Positive Effect",
  neg_legend_title       = "Negative Effect",
  low_color              = "blue",
  mid_color              = "white",
  high_color             = "red",
  save_dir               = ".",
  file_name              = "Adjusted_P_Value_Heatmap.pdf",
  fig_width              = 8.5,
  fig_height             = 11,
  title                  = "Adjusted P-Value Heatmap",
  landscape              = FALSE,
  show_legend            = TRUE
)
```

### Notes

- Input data is a wide-format table produced by `CreateSigBetaTable()` in `"continuous_signed"` mode.
- `data_col_indices` are numeric column indices for the area columns; `descriptor_col_indices` for the y-axis label column.
- Used by `createHeatMapsFromLmerAreaAnalysis()` for `heatmap_type = "activation"`.

\newpage

## `create_omnibus_heatmap`

Generates a single-color green gradient heatmap for unsigned p-values (e.g., from omnibus F-tests). Darker green = smaller p-value. Supports log scaling (default) and significance asterisks.

### Usage

```{r}
create_omnibus_heatmap(
  table_data,
  data_col_indices,
  descriptor_col_indices,
  scale_type             = "log",
  log_power              = 0.2,
  legend_breaks          = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.50),
  significance_threshold = 0.05,
  asterisk_size          = 6,
  low_color              = "darkgreen",
  high_color             = "white",
  save_dir               = ".",
  file_name              = "Omnibus_Heatmap.pdf",
  fig_width              = 8.5,
  fig_height             = 11,
  title                  = "Omnibus P-Value Heatmap",
  landscape              = FALSE,
  show_legend            = TRUE
)
```

## `create_posthoc_heatmap`

Extension of `create_pvalue_heatmap` that renders NA cells (untested ROIs where the omnibus gate was not passed) as grey tiles.

### Usage

```{r}
create_posthoc_heatmap(
  table_data,
  data_col_indices,
  descriptor_col_indices,
  scale_type             = "linear",
  log_power              = 0.2,
  legend_breaks          = c(-0.05, -0.01, -0.001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05),
  significance_threshold = 0.05,
  asterisk_size          = 6,
  pos_legend_title       = "Positive Effect",
  neg_legend_title       = "Negative Effect",
  low_color              = "blue",
  mid_color              = "white",
  high_color             = "red",
  untested_color         = "grey80",
  save_dir               = ".",
  file_name              = "PostHoc_Heatmap.pdf",
  fig_width              = 8.5,
  fig_height             = 11,
  title                  = "Post-Hoc P-Value Heatmap",
  landscape              = FALSE,
  show_legend            = TRUE
)
```

## `create_forced_color_heatmap`

Renders a heatmap using a discrete color mapping (e.g., `-1` = blue, `0` = white, `1` = red). Used by `createHeatMapsFromLmerAreaAnalysis()` for the discrete effect tables.

### Usage

```{r}
create_forced_color_heatmap(
  table_data,
  data_col_indices,
  descriptor_col_indices,
  color_mapping = c("-1" = "blue", "0" = "white", "1" = "red"),
  save_dir      = ".",
  file_name     = "Forced_Color_Heatmap.pdf",
  fig_width     = 8.5,
  fig_height    = 11,
  title         = "Significance Direction Heatmap",
  landscape     = FALSE,
  show_legend   = TRUE
)
```

\newpage

## `create_heatmap_legend`

Renders just the legend that the chFnirs heatmap functions produce, with no panel or axes, and saves it to its own PDF. Designed for publication panels where multiple heatmaps share a single legend rather than each carrying its own embedded copy. Pair with `show_legend = FALSE` on the heatmap calls themselves and `heatmap_height(..., show_legend = FALSE)` to drop the row-height floor.

### Usage

```{r}
create_heatmap_legend(
  show_pos          = TRUE,
  show_neg          = TRUE,
  show_not_tested   = FALSE,
  scale_type        = "linear",
  log_power         = 0.2,
  pos_legend_breaks = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05),
  neg_legend_breaks = c(-0.05, -0.01, -0.001),
  pos_value_limits  = c(0, 1),
  neg_value_limits  = c(-1, 0),
  pos_legend_title  = "Positive Effect",
  neg_legend_title  = "Negative Effect",
  not_tested_label  = "Not tested\n(omnibus n.s.)",
  pos_color         = "red",
  neg_color         = "blue",
  mid_color         = "white",
  not_tested_color  = "grey80",
  fig_width         = 3,
  fig_height        = 5,
  save_dir          = ".",
  file_name         = "Heatmap_Legend.pdf"
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `show_pos` | logical | `TRUE` | Include the positive colorbar. |
| `show_neg` | logical | `TRUE` | Include the negative colorbar. |
| `show_not_tested` | logical | `FALSE` | Include the not-tested swatch. |
| `scale_type` | string | `"linear"` | One of `"linear"`, `"log"` (p-value modes; transformation `1 - |p|^log_power` lands in `[0, 1]`), or `"none"` (no transformation; breaks used as colorbar positions directly — for effect-size legends). Must match the heatmap's `scale_type`. |
| `log_power` | numeric | `0.2` | Must match the heatmap's `log_power` when `scale_type = "log"`. |
| `pos_legend_breaks` | numeric | `c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05)` | P-values (or effect-size values when `scale_type = "none"`) labeled on the positive bar. |
| `neg_legend_breaks` | numeric | `c(-0.05, -0.01, -0.001)` | P-values (or negative effect-size values) on the negative bar. |
| `pos_value_limits` | numeric | `c(0, 1)` | Positive colorbar domain. For p-value modes the default is correct. For `scale_type = "none"`, set to match the heatmap (e.g., `c(0, 1)` for Cohen's d, `c(0, 0.2)` for partial η²). |
| `neg_value_limits` | numeric | `c(-1, 0)` | Negative colorbar domain. Override for `scale_type = "none"` (e.g., `c(-1, 0)` for Cohen's d). |
| `pos_legend_title` | string | `"Positive Effect"` | Pass `"p-value"` for the omnibus legend, or e.g. `"Cohen's d (+)"` for an effect-size legend. |
| `neg_legend_title` | string | `"Negative Effect"` | |
| `not_tested_label` | string | `"Not tested\n(omnibus n.s.)"` | Newline matches the embedded post-hoc legend. |
| `pos_color` | string | `"red"` | High-end color for the positive bar. Pass `"darkgreen"` for omnibus, `"darkorange"` for sequential effect-size. |
| `neg_color` | string | `"blue"` | Low-end color for the negative bar. |
| `mid_color` | string | `"white"` | Midpoint color of both bars. |
| `not_tested_color` | string | `"grey80"` | Swatch color. |
| `fig_width`, `fig_height` | numeric | `3`, `5` | Output PDF dimensions. |
| `save_dir`, `file_name` | string | `"."`, `"Heatmap_Legend.pdf"` | Output path. |

### Common patterns

```{r}
# Activation legend (positive + negative, no not-tested)
create_heatmap_legend(show_pos = TRUE, show_neg = TRUE,
                      show_not_tested = FALSE)

# Omnibus legend (single green colorbar)
create_heatmap_legend(
  show_pos = TRUE, show_neg = FALSE, show_not_tested = FALSE,
  pos_color = "darkgreen",
  pos_legend_title = "p-value",
  pos_legend_breaks = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.50)
)

# Post-hoc legend (full stack)
create_heatmap_legend(show_pos = TRUE, show_neg = TRUE,
                      show_not_tested = TRUE)

# Effect-size legend, Cohen's d (diverging, no transformation)
create_heatmap_legend(
  show_pos = TRUE, show_neg = TRUE, show_not_tested = FALSE,
  scale_type = "none",
  pos_value_limits = c(0, 1),
  neg_value_limits = c(-1, 0),
  pos_legend_breaks = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8),
  neg_legend_breaks = c(-0.8, -0.5, -0.2),
  pos_legend_title = "Cohen's d (+)",
  neg_legend_title = "Cohen's d (-)"
)

# Effect-size legend, partial eta-squared (sequential)
create_heatmap_legend(
  show_pos = TRUE, show_neg = FALSE, show_not_tested = FALSE,
  scale_type = "none",
  pos_value_limits = c(0, 0.2),
  pos_legend_breaks = c(0.01, 0.06, 0.14),
  pos_legend_title = "partial eta-sq",
  pos_color = "darkorange"
)
```

### Publication workflow

```{r}
fig_dir <- "paper/figures"

# Render N heatmaps without legends
for (chrom in c("hbo", "cbsi")) {
  df_sub <- subset(df.posthoc, type == chrom)
  create_posthoc_heatmap(
    df_sub, ..., show_legend = FALSE,
    fig_height = heatmap_height(df_sub, show_legend = FALSE),
    save_dir = fig_dir,
    file_name = sprintf("Panel_%s.pdf", chrom)
  )
}

# Export one shared legend
create_heatmap_legend(
  show_pos = TRUE, show_neg = TRUE, show_not_tested = TRUE,
  save_dir = fig_dir,
  file_name = "Shared_Legend_PostHoc.pdf"
)
```

\newpage

## `plot_simple_slopes`

For each significant type x area cell in a BH-corrected omnibus table, produces a pair of simple-slopes plots for a continuous x continuous interaction: one with `var1` on the x-axis and `var2` as the moderator (at Mean $\pm$ SD levels), and one with roles reversed.

### Usage

```{r}
plot_simple_slopes(
  omnibus_df, data, formula, area_col,
  var1, var2,
  effect_pattern   = NULL,
  type_col         = "type",
  model,
  vcov             = NULL,
  p_col            = "p_bh",
  p_threshold      = 0.05,
  gate             = TRUE,
  mod_sd_levels    = c(-1, 0, 1),
  line_colors      = NULL,
  y_label          = NULL,
  pdf_prefix       = NULL,
  output_dir       = ".",
  split_by_type    = TRUE,
  show_points      = FALSE,
  show_ci          = TRUE,
  x_label          = NULL,
  moderator_label  = NULL,
  panel_labels     = NULL,
  fig_width        = 7,
  fig_height       = 5
)
```

### Key arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `var1`, `var2` | string | | The two continuous variables forming the interaction. |
| `effect_pattern` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Regex for matching omnibus effects. Auto-generates from var1/var2. |
| `gate` | logical | `TRUE` | Only plot significant cells. |
| `mod_sd_levels` | numeric vector | `c(-1, 0, 1)` | SD units for moderator levels. |
| `y_label` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Auto-detected from formula LHS. |
| `pdf_prefix` | string/NULL | `NULL` | If non-NULL, writes multi-page PDFs. |
| `show_points` | logical | `FALSE` | Overlay raw subject data. Default FALSE because moderator slices are synthetic. |
| `show_ci` | logical | `TRUE` | Pointwise 95% confidence band (from `emmeans`) behind each line, filled with the line color at alpha 0.15. `FALSE` draws lines alone. |
| `line_colors` | string vector/NULL | `NULL` | One color per value of `mod_sd_levels`; wrong length errors. `NULL` interpolates blue, gray, red across sorted levels (-1, 0, 1 give `steelblue`, `grey45`, `tomato`). For lines alone in a grey, blue and navy scheme use `show_ci = FALSE, line_colors = c("grey65", "steelblue", "navyblue")`. |
| `x_label` | named string vector/NULL | `NULL` | x-axis labels keyed by `var1`/`var2`, since the variables swap axes between pages. Unnamed variables keep their names. |
| `moderator_label` | named string vector/NULL | `NULL` | Legend titles keyed by `var1`/`var2`. A named moderator also shortens its level labels to `-1SD`, `Mean`, `+1SD`. |
| `panel_labels` | named string vector/NULL | `NULL` | Facet-strip labels keyed by factor level. Unmatched names error. |

### Return value

Nested list of ggplot objects organized by type. Each element is `list(page_A = <ggplot>, page_B = <ggplot>)`.

\newpage

## `plot_slope_lines`

Companion plot for `run_slopes_vs_zero()` and `run_gated_slopes()`. For every significant row, draws the fitted slope line(s) with optional CI ribbons and raw-data overlay. Auto-detects activation vs. post-hoc mode from the `posthoc_type` column.

### Usage

```{r}
plot_slope_lines(
  results_df, data, formula, area_col, trend_var,
  type_col      = "type",
  model,
  vcov          = NULL,
  p_col         = "p_bh",
  p_threshold   = 0.05,
  by_factor     = NULL,
  suffix        = "SlopeDiff",
  show_ci       = TRUE,
  show_points   = TRUE,
  point_alpha   = 0.4,
  pdf_prefix    = NULL,
  output_dir    = ".",
  split_by_type = TRUE,
  fig_width     = 7,
  fig_height    = 5
)
```

### Key arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `trend_var` | string | | Continuous moderator (x-axis of every plot). |
| `by_factor` | string/NULL | `NULL` | Level-column for activation mode. |
| `suffix` | string | `"SlopeDiff"` | Suffix to strip when parsing `predictor` labels. |
| `show_ci` | logical | `TRUE` | Draw pointwise 95% CI ribbon. |
| `show_points` | logical | `TRUE` | Overlay raw subject data, filtered per line. |
| `point_alpha` | numeric | `0.4` | Transparency of data points. |

### Notes

- **Activation mode** (no `posthoc_type` column): each significant row = one slope line.
- **Post-hoc mode** (`posthoc_type` present): each significant row = two slope lines (the pairwise contrast).
- Three-way decompositions parse the conditioning level from the `predictor` column.

\newpage

# Utilities

## `getBHvalues`

Calculates Benjamini--Hochberg FDR-adjusted p-values. Supports grouping by one or more columns so that separate families of tests are controlled independently.

### Usage

```{r}
getBHvalues(df_data, group_col = NULL, p_val_col)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `df_data` | data.frame | | Input data. |
| `group_col` | string/vector/NULL | `NULL` | Column(s) defining independent families. |
| `p_val_col` | string | | P-value column name. |

### Return value

The input data frame with an added `pBH` column.

### Notes

When multiple columns are supplied for `group_col`, uses `interaction()` internally to build a single grouping factor. Single-row groups copy the raw p-value as the BH-adjusted value.

## `getQvalues`

Wrapper for `qvalue::qvalue()` to calculate Storey's q-values from p-values. Supports grouping.

### Usage

```{r}
getQvalues(df_data, group_col = NULL, p_val_col)
```

### Return value

The input data frame with an added `qVal` column.

\newpage

## `compute_cohens_d`

Computes Cohen's d by dividing a vector of estimates by the residual standard deviation of the fitted model. The sign of d matches the sign of the estimate (since $\sigma$ is always positive).

### Usage

```{r}
compute_cohens_d(model, estimate_col)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `model` | fitted model | Must support `stats::sigma()`. |
| `estimate_col` | numeric vector | Marginal means, contrasts, or slopes on the response scale. |

### Return value

Numeric vector of Cohen's d values. `NA_real_` if $\sigma$ is zero, NA, or undefined.

## `compute_partial_eta_sq`

Computes partial eta-squared ($SS_{effect} / (SS_{effect} + SS_{residual})$) for every row of an ANOVA table. Auto-detects the sum-of-squares column name (`"Sum Sq"` or `"SS"`).

### Usage

```{r}
compute_partial_eta_sq(anova_table)
```

### Return value

Numeric vector of partial $\eta^2$ values. `NA_real_` if no SS column or no Residuals row is found.

## `has_tested_results`

Gate helper for conditional heatmap rendering. Returns `TRUE` when a results data frame has at least one non-NA p-value (`p_bon` checked first, then `p_value`).

### Usage

```{r}
has_tested_results(df)
```

### Return value

Single logical value.

\newpage

## `standardize_emmeans_columns`

Renames columns of an `emmeans` output data frame to the canonical chFnirs snake\_case schema.

### Usage

```{r}
standardize_emmeans_columns(df, mode, trend_var = NULL)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `df` | data.frame | From `as.data.frame()` on an emmeans result. |
| `mode` | string | `"marginal"` (emmean $\to$ estimate), `"contrast"` (p.value $\to$ p\_bon), or `"trend"` (trend\_var.trend $\to$ estimate). |
| `trend_var` | string/NULL | Required when `mode = "trend"`. |

### Common renames (all modes)

`SE` $\to$ `se`, `t.ratio` / `z.ratio` $\to$ `statistic`. Factor-level columns and `df` pass through untouched.

## `write_results_by_type`

Convenience wrapper around `write.csv()` that splits a long-format table by its `type` column and writes one CSV per type into its own subdirectory.

### Usage

```{r}
write_results_by_type(
  df,
  filename,
  output_dir    = ".",
  split_by_type = TRUE,
  type_col      = "type",
  row.names     = FALSE,
  ...
)
```

## `sort_rois_anatomically`

Reorders a character vector of ROI names according to a neuroanatomical hierarchy: frontal $\to$ precentral $\to$ parietal $\to$ angular $\to$ temporal, then superior medial $\to$ superior $\to$ middle $\to$ inferior, then left before right.

### Usage

```{r}
sort_rois_anatomically(roi_vector)
```

### Return value

Character vector of sorted ROI names. Unrecognized ROIs are placed at the end with a warning.

## `sort_fnirs_channels_by_name`

Channel-side companion to `sort_rois_anatomically`. Parses fNIRS channel names of the form `"Ch_<source>_<detector>"`, looks up source/detector positions in a `digpts.txt` file, groups channels into anterior--posterior bands (gap-detected by default), and sorts left-to-right within each band. Returns the input names in plotting order; per-channel diagnostics (parsed coordinates, band assignment, final order index) are attached as `attr(result, "diagnostics")`.

### Usage

```{r}
sort_fnirs_channels_by_name(
  channel_names, digpts_path,
  n_bands = 2, y_breaks = NULL,
  channel_parser = NULL, verbose = FALSE
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `channel_names` | char vec | | Channel names (e.g., `c("Ch_1_1", "Ch_2_3", ...)`). |
| `digpts_path` | string | | Path to a `digpts.txt` file with `s1: x y z`-style lines. |
| `n_bands` | integer | `2` | Number of anterior--posterior bands. |
| `y_breaks` | numeric/NULL | `NULL` | Explicit band boundaries (overrides `n_bands`). |
| `channel_parser` | function/NULL | `NULL` | Custom parser; default handles `Ch_<s>_<d>`. |
| `verbose` | logical | `FALSE` | Print orientation and band summary. |

### Return value

Character vector of input channel names in plotting order, with diagnostics attached as an attribute.

## Pluggable area sorters

`createHeatMapsFromLmerAreaAnalysis()` and `create_effect_size_heatmap()` accept any sort function that satisfies the contract `function(names, ...) -> ordered names`. Both `sort_rois_anatomically()` and `sort_fnirs_channels_by_name()` satisfy it, and they are interchangeable behind the heatmap `area_order` argument. Custom sorters (e.g., by effect size, by region size, by Brodmann area) plug in the same way --- precompute the order, pass it as `area_order`, and the heatmap will render columns in that order. When `area_order = NULL`, columns appear in the order they occur in `results_df`.

## `heatmap_height`

Returns a `fig_height` value (in inches) scaled so each heatmap row keeps roughly the same visual height regardless of how many predictors are in the data. Reserves a fixed margin for title, rotated x-axis labels, and plot padding, then divides the remaining chart strip evenly among the rows up to `full_n`; caps at `full_height` thereafter.

### Usage

```{r}
heatmap_height(
  df,
  full_height     = 8.5,
  full_n          = 10,
  margin          = 2,
  show_legend     = TRUE,
  min_height      = NULL,
  pred_col        = "predictor",
  removeIntercept = TRUE
)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `df` | data.frame | | Long-format data whose `pred_col` becomes heatmap rows. |
| `full_height` | numeric | `8.5` | Figure height in inches at and above the cap. |
| `full_n` | numeric | `10` | Row count at which the figure reaches `full_height`. Increase for smaller rows. |
| `margin` | numeric | `2` | Inches reserved for non-chart elements. |
| `show_legend` | logical | `TRUE` | Whether the heatmap will render with its side legend. Used to pick the default `min_height`. |
| `min_height` | numeric/NULL | `NULL` | Floor on the returned height. `NULL` resolves to `5` if `show_legend` is `TRUE` (fits the typical legend stack) or `3` if `FALSE`. Override with an explicit value. |
| `pred_col` | string | `"predictor"` | Name of predictor column in `df`. |
| `removeIntercept` | logical | `TRUE` | Drop predictors whose name contains `"Intercept"`. |

### Typical use

```{r}
createHeatMapsFromLmerAreaAnalysis(
  results_df = df.posthoc, area_col = "area", group_col = "type",
  sigValue_col = "p_bon", dv_col = "estimate",
  area_order = sort_rois_anatomically(unique(df.posthoc$area)),
  fig_height = heatmap_height(df.posthoc),
  output_prefix = "PostHoc"
)
```

## `shorten_string`

Replaces each word in a string with its first `num_letters` characters. Optionally removes specified substrings first.

### Usage

```{r}
shorten_string(input_str, num_letters = 2, stringsToRemove = NULL)
```

\newpage

## `run_lmer_analysis_by_area` (deprecated)

**\[Deprecated\]**

Original area-wise lmer omnibus function. Superseded by `run_omnibus_by_area()` which supports both lmer and lm models, robust covariance, and the unified output schema. Calls produce a deprecation warning via the `lifecycle` package pointing to the replacement.

# Internal functions

## `iterate_by_area`

Shared iteration engine used internally by all the area-wise analysis functions. Loops over unique `type_col` x `area_col` combinations, subsets data, fits a model via `fit_fn`, extracts results via `extract_fn`, and row-binds the output. Errors for individual cells are caught with `tryCatch` and logged; the loop continues.

### Usage

```{r}
iterate_by_area(data, area_col, type_col, min_rows,
                fit_fn, extract_fn, fn_label)
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `fit_fn` | closure | `function(df_cell)` returning a fitted model. |
| `extract_fn` | closure | `function(fit, df_cell)` returning a per-cell data.frame. |
| `fn_label` | string | Used in error messages to identify the calling function. |

### Notes

This function is `@keywords internal` and is not exported. Users should call the public wrappers.
